Mark, can I ask you something? My daughter wants to visit Boston in December.
Great idea! But December is very cold. She should take a big coat.
Ha, yes! And hotels in Boston are expensive. That's a problem.
She could stay in Cambridge. It's near Boston, and it's cheaper.
Good idea. And the plane ticket?
She should buy it early. In October, tickets are cheaper.
Okay. She wants to save money.

Hi, Érica. It's Mark. I have more advice for your daughter. In Boston, she should walk the Freedom Trail. It's free, and it's the best walk in the city. She could also visit Harvard, in Cambridge. For food, she could try clam chowder. It's a famous soup in Boston. And she shouldn't rent a car. The traffic is terrible, and parking is very expensive. She should take the subway. Okay, talk soon!

Hello, and welcome to Ask Anna. Today's letter is from Paulo. He writes: I'm always stressed at work. I have too many projects, and I can't sleep. What should I do? Well, Paulo, here are my ideas. First, you should talk to your boss. Maybe you could finish one project before you start a new one. Second, you could take a short walk at lunch. Why don't you leave your phone on your desk? And at night, you shouldn't answer emails. Your bed is for sleeping, not for working! Good luck, Paulo.
